results.title: JoyNews’ Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi wins GJA award for domestic tourism reporting
results.content: JoyNews’ Ahafo Regional Correspondent, Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi, has won the Best Reporter on Domestic Tourism award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards. He was recognised for his article, “Speaking Ghana to the world: How indigenous languages can power tourism and economic growth,” at the awards ceremony held in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The Awards Committee, chaired by former Graphic Communications Group Editor Kobby Asmah, commended the report for demonstrating the value of development journalism and highlighting the role of Ghana’s indigenous languages in promoting tourism and economic growth. In its citation, the committee said the article drew attention to the potential of local languages as a tool for economic transformation.

results.title: Fifi Kwetey, Yameen, Ako Gunn go unopposed in NDC national executive race

The list, revealed on Monday, November 9, shows that four candidates are seeking the position of National Chairman, while Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, Joseph Yameen and Ako Gunn are going unopposed for their respective positions.

results.title: COP31: Africa makes progress on adoption of key supplementary priorities on agenda
results.content: COP31 must mark the definitive transition from negotiated promises to tangible financial delivery, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has urged world leaders in a decisive call as the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) opened in Antalya on Monday. Speaking on behalf of the continent at the opening plenary in Antalya, AGN Chair, Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, emphasized that Africa’s ability to fulfill its climate commitments rests entirely on the immediate mobilization of scaled-up, predictable climate finance. Aligning the African block with the Group of 77 and China, Dr. Amoah declared that an implementation-focused summit must be a summit that delivers on finance, setting a firm tone for the two-week negotiations hosted by Türkiye with Australia presiding over negotiations.

results.title: Researchers urge government to fund Ghana-focused health studies and apply findings
results.content: Researchers and health professionals have called for increased government investment in local health research, warning that inadequate funding and the limited application of research findings could undermine efforts to address Ghana’s healthcare challenges. They say stronger support for indigenous research and closer collaboration between scientists, policymakers and healthcare practitioners are necessary to ensure evidence informs public policy and improves service delivery. The concerns were raised at the second Research Dissemination Day organised by HopeXchange Medical Centre, where experts also highlighted the challenges facing young researchers and the difficulties of translating scientific findings into practical interventions.

results.title: How Ghana can build an economy that produces more with her abundant resources
results.content: In September 2026, it took me more than twelve hours to travel the 266 kilometres from Nkroful to Kumasi through the important mining towns of Tarkwa, Bogosu, Dunkwa-on-Offin, Ayanfuri and Obuasi. In 2025, I compared Accra–Kumasi trips of at least six hours with a three-hour journey from Abidjan to Yamoussoukro over a similar distance. These were individual journeys, but they raise a question for every producer who depends on a road. How much of a working day can you afford to lose getting goods to market? results.title: EOCO says visit to Wontumi’s property was for valuation, not a raid
results.content: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has denied reports that its officers ransacked a property belonging to the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi. In a statement issued on Monday, November 9, 2026, the Office said its officers, accompanied by officials from the Lands Commission, visited the Tema property to take coordinates and measurements for a professional valuation. EOCO said the exercise formed part of due process following the freezing of the property, which it said was confirmed by a court last year. “The said property was frozen by EOCO and confirmed by the Court last year. As part of due process, EOCO and Lands Commission officials were at the property to pick the coordinates and measurements to enable Lands Commission to conduct a professional valuation,” the statement said.
